pages.name: A pump's curve
pages.text: A pump's curve plots the [[head]] it gives, how high it could lift water, against its flow. A low flow gives a high head, and a high flow a low head.

Low flow, high head; high flow, low head.

pages.name: Up, then across
pages.text: To read the head at a flow, go up from the flow to the curve, then across. Up from 10 m³/h reads 19 m. Slide the marker to read others.

pages.name: Read the head
pages.task: What head does this pump give at 20 m³/h?
pages.why: Go up from 20 m³/h to the curve, then across to the head axis. It meets the axis 4 small squares above 10, and each is 1 m, so 14 m.

pages.name: Find the flow
pages.task: The pump must give 20 m of head. Drag the marker to the flow that gives it.
pages.why: Go across from 20 m on the head axis to the curve, then straight down. It lands on 5 m³/h. As a check, up from 5 m³/h and across reads 20 m.

pages.name: More flow
pages.task: The flow goes up from 10 to 20 m³/h. What happens to the head?
pages.why: Up and across from 10 m³/h reads 19 m, and from 20 m³/h reads 14 m. So the head falls 19 − 14 = 5 m.
